main_text.p: mnia, per omnia & in omnibus nobis, Ephes. 4. 6. Ipsius opus sumus, conditi in Christo Iesu ad opera bona, quæ præparauit Deus vt in eis versaremur. Ephes. 2. 10.

Quotiescunq; vero Dominū tuū Iehoua, corde credis & ore confiteris, hac laudem tibi illi deferre statues, quòd sit[?] is ipse à quo conditus es, & vitæ dono, illiusq; tuendæ præsidijs benignè instructus: quòd ab eodem redemtus sis à potestate tenebrarum, & translatus in regnum lucis, quòd is te sanctificet ad æternam vitam: deniq; quòd tibi benedictionis spiritualis & temporalis, vnicus & benignissimus auctor sit: quòd te custodiat, & ab omni malo tueatur.
Hæc autem diuinæ bonitatis documenta, accendere & fouere debet in corde tuo, reuerentiam erga Dominum Deum tuum, Malach. i. 6. & studium eidem promtè & cōstanter obediendi.

4. Quòd deniq; certæ Genti potissimū, denunciata sunt onera illa. De Edomæa) Synechdoche est, Regionem enim pro gente eam inhabitate, sumsit Propheta noster. Cæterum quum vobis Edomiticæ gentis origine, regione, religione, ingenio, rebus gestis, odio aduersus Iudæos fratres, ex Biblicis historijs, constare possit[?], non insti-tuam de ea gente tractationem hoc loco &

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "sit" in "quòd sit is ipse" is printed with a letter that could be f; "posit" in the last paragraph is read as written, with a possible long-s double. "Ephes. 2. 10" is printed "z.io" in the old figures; the numbers are read as 2 and 10. "De Edomæa)" has a closing parenthesis as printed. The first word "mnia" is cut at the top edge of the scan and the initial letter is not visible, so the fragment is kept as it stands. The number "19" is read from a worn figure at the top right.
